assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework are the core of modern monetary-policy analysis and are used in central banks worldwide. Staggered pricing and contracts, the Taylor rule and the Woodford synthesis changed both theory and practice. The impact is very broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: The field has many contributors, so the credit has to be trimmed. Calvo (time-dependent pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and policy rules) and Woodford (the microfounded policy framework) give a defensible core. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are important for estimation and extension, and omitting them is a real cost.
assessment.maturity: The work is four decades old and fully tested, with a long record of use in policy. Timing is not a concern. The 2022 prize for banking and financial crises does not overlap with it.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer a narrower or different trio from this crowded field
Post-2008 criticism of the framework and the rise of heterogeneous-agent extensions might dilute the case
I rely on my own knowledge of the literature and have not independently verified the credit attributions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson, Tabellini and Besley built the formal, empirically tested framework for how electoral rules, constitutions, state capacity and fiscal institutions shape policy and development. The research programme is coherent and deep, and it shaped a whole field of political economics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini (the political-economics synthesis and the constitutions work) and Besley (state capacity and accountability) form a natural cluster. Credit is fairly clear, though Acemoglu, Robinson and others work in adjacent territory.
assessment.maturity: The work runs from the 1990s to the 2010s and is well confirmed and widely taught. The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity partly overlaps in theme but not in the core contributions.
uncertainties: The 2024 institutions prize may reduce the committee's appetite for a related political-economy award
Some of the empirical constitutional-effects results are debated
Persson's past Academy ties need to be handled transparently, though conflicts are disclosed rather than adjudicated here

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection reshaped international trade theory and empirics after the Krugman new-trade-theory era. The Melitz model, with Helpman's work on heterogeneous firms and trade, became the workhorse for quantitative trade and welfare analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the clear anchor. Helpman made central contributions on firm-level trade, FDI and organisation. Redding is a strong extender, but a two-person award keeps the credit tight.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation, with extensive empirical work and policy use. Trade has not been honoured since 2008, so timing is plausible.
uncertainties: Helpman also appears in a separate candidate on political-economy trade models, so the committee may weigh a combined case
Whether the model's welfare implications are robust across the literature on gains from trade

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural demand estimation with differentiated products and dynamic industry models is the standard toolkit in empirical industrial organisation. It is used in merger review, antitrust and regulation, so both the methods impact and the policy impact are large.
assessment.attribution: The BLP approach (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is the clean core. Pakes also has distinct dynamic-game and productivity-estimation contributions. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are significant but are omitted to keep the credit tight.
assessment.maturity: The BLP method dates from the mid-1990s and has been in heavy use for decades. It is a mature contribution.
uncertainties: The credit is spread across many contributors, with some arguable omissions such as Bresnahan
Whether the committee sees this as methodological toolbuilding or as a conceptual discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The top-incomes and long-run distribution data reset the empirical foundation for inequality research and reoriented public debate and subsequent academic work. The contribution is largely data construction and measurement, with some theoretical claims that are contested.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the originators of the top-income series, and Zucman extended them to wealth and offshore holdings. A two-person award would favour the original data programme. Conceptual claims such as r>g are more disputed than the measurement itself.
assessment.maturity: The top-income work dates from 2003 onward and has been replicated across countries. Wealth-distribution estimates remain debated.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes over wealth-inequality measurement
The committee may judge the measurement contribution less fundamental than conceptual advances
Saez also appears in a public-economics candidate, so there is some overlap in attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology, the education-technology race and the China-shock evidence changed how economists understand labour demand, polarisation and wage inequality. The findings are central to debates on technology, trade and work, and they influenced a large empirical literature.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central across the task framework and the trade-shock work. Katz is central to the skill-premium and education-technology race literature. Hanson is co-lead on the trade-shock evidence. Dorn is a significant co-author but omitted. Acemoglu's earlier prize overlaps conceptually with the task framework.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 1992 to 2016 and has been widely replicated, though the interpretation of the China shock is still evolving.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2024 prize on technology and institutions
Debates over magnitudes in the trade-shock literature
Whether three is the right set given the multiple distinct contributions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Misallocation across firms offers a disciplined, quantifiable account of cross-country income and TFP differences. It linked micro-level frictions to aggregate outcomes, and became a standard framework in growth, development and macro.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the empirical anchor and Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) the theoretical one. Rogerson is not in the credited names, so the attribution is incomplete. The three credited names form a reasonable group.
assessment.maturity: The literature is about 15 years old and has been actively extended. Measurement concerns (markups, adjustment costs, measurement error) mean some quantitative conclusions are less settled.
uncertainties: Debate about whether measured dispersion reflects true distortions or mismeasurement
Rogerson's absence from the credited names weakens the attribution
The 2025 prize on growth through innovation may reduce appetite for a growth-related award soon after

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Manski founded partial identification, clarifying what can be learned from data under credible rather than convenient assumptions. The framework also shaped thinking on the reflection problem, treatment choice and policy analysis under uncertainty, so the conceptual contribution is deep.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear originator. Tamer and Molinari are important developers of inference and moment inequalities, but later and more technical. A single-laureate proposal reflects the clarity of founding credit.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work dates from around 1989 onward. It has gradually gained wide methodological influence, although applied adoption is narrower than for the 2021 causal-inference work.
uncertainties: Applied adoption is narrower than that of other econometric advances
The 2021 prize already recognised credible causal inference, which may affect the committee's appetite for another econometrics award
Whether a single-laureate prize or a trio including Tamer and Molinari would be preferred
